title: Development and validation of a noninvasive machine learning model using urinary extracellular vesicle physical parameters for prostate cancer diagnosis.
summary: Machine learning used physical measurements of urinary extracellular vesicles to distinguish prostate cancer from benign prostatic hyperplasia in a three-hospital biopsy cohort.
ai_technology: Five ML algorithms use urinary extracellular-vesicle physical measurements in 222 biopsy-indicated patients recruited at three centers (65 pathology-confirmed cancer, 157 BPH); model predicts cancer status as a possible adjunct biomarker.
organization: The Second Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University; Beijing Shijitan Hospital; Capital Medical University

evidence.tested: The study compared five algorithms against biopsy pathology in 222 patients, including 65 with cancer. It drew its 67-patient test set from the same cohort.
evidence.unknown: No external-site test was reported. The study did not establish whether the model improves biopsy decisions.
evidence.ai_role: Five ML algorithms use urinary extracellular-vesicle physical measurements in 222 biopsy-indicated patients recruited at three centers (65 pathology-confirmed cancer, 157 BPH); model predicts cancer status as a possible adjunct biomarker.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
